executiveSummary: GM1952's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 61,387 residents, 91 neighbourhoods, 27 BAG places, 62 settlement labels, four railway stations and eleven NWB border links are internally coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only 17 residents (-0.028%) and is reconciled without rewriting source observations. The complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Midden-Groningen is a low-lying, pump-dependent municipality in the Duurswold water system, with polders 2–3 m below NAP, raised boezem channels, Schildmeer storage and discharge toward Farmsum. The canonical coastal run produces 1.276793 of legacy depth-like amplitude and up to 29,085 affected resident-equivalents without selecting a sea level, defence failure, canal/boezem state, connected footprint or dewatering path; the major-river run is exactly zero at every checkpoint but tests only the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel family and cannot clear Duurswold, Winschoterdiep, Eemskanaal, canal-dike, polder or pluvial mechanisms. Five reviewed induced seismic origins fall inside GM1952 in the rolling KNMI snapshot, including Sappemeer M1.58 and Woudbloem M1.99. Yet a focused replay at the reviewed Sappemeer origin places its containing neighbourhood fiftieth of 91, behind the same generic rank used by unrelated hazards. A focused ignition in Slochteren Natuurgebied likewise ranks only fifteenth despite the municipality's 1,700-hectare 't Roegwold nature complex. Exact eight-service and 72-hour recovery values omit the documented water-control chain, hazardous facilities at Foxhol/Hoogezand, four-station rail corridor, A7/N33 cross-boundary dependencies, external acute care, dispersed villages, utility topology and action/resource state. Public observations and registers remain context only; Unknown and NoData must never be presented as zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1952 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1952 as Midden-Groningen in Groningen and reports 61,387 residents, density 221/km2, 24.2% aged 65 or older and 10,641 one-person households. The generated centre [6.799621948695595, 53.179012360445] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Ninety-one neighbourhood rows in 21 districts sum to 61,370 residents, 17 below the municipality total (-0.028%); households sum to 28,660 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 14,855. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 61,387 without altering source values.

BAG supplies 27 current woonplaatsen and BRT supplies 62 settlement labels: 24 woonkernen, 27 buurtschappen, six deelkernen and five gehuchten. All label points are contained in the generalized municipality boundary; labels remain neither occupancy nor service/catchment footprints.

Most statistic fields cover all 91 neighbourhoods, but home value covers 67, household size 86, cars per household 61, several benefit/access fields 68–80, housing/tenure 69 and district heat/public charging 0. Null, suppression, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current municipal earthquake-impact and 2023 climate-adaptation programme
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; Klimaatadaptatieplan 2023 with four-year review cycle
supports: The municipality states that Midden-Groningen belongs to the earthquake area and that almost everywhere in the municipality experiences consequences of gas extraction. It provides current routes to damage, strengthening, health, liveability and personal-help organizations and identifies the municipal Team Gevolgen Gas- en Zoutwinning.

The linked climate-adaptation programme addresses heavy rain, heat, drought and sea-level rise and includes sewer adjustment, water retention and drinking-water conservation. Programme intent is not an incident rainfall field, sewer capacity, groundwater state, inundation depth or completion record.

A municipal report on the 29 August 2026 fire at TenneT's Meeden high-voltage station says the station was taken out of service preventively and supply was rerouted, with no reported electricity outage. That dated incident demonstrates a switching mechanism, not guaranteed redundancy, present state or a future restoration curve.

The public pages are current documentary evidence with municipality scope and no standard redistribution licence or machine event cadence identified. Projects, support routes and historic/recent incident outcomes do not quantify current vulnerability or response capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and Duurswold/Schildmeer water-system description
evidenceSources.edition: Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and Kanalen Duurswold background document; public documents inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The authority places Duurswold between Delfzijl, Groningen and Hoogezand-Sappemeer. Polders lie 2–3 m below NAP and continue to subside through gas extraction and peat oxidation, while the Siddeburen–Slochteren–Harkstede ribbon is approximately at NAP on a sand ridge.

The boezem consists of Slochterdiep and branches, Afwateringskanaal Duurswold and Schildmeer, raised through the central landscape. Pumps lift surrounding polder water into it; excess is discharged at Farmsum through a sluice and sea pumping station, and water can be supplied from Eemskanaal during shortage.

The Kanalen Duurswold document identifies Slochterdiep, Scharmer Ae, Woltersumer Aa, De Groeve and Schildmeer as connected water bodies used for conveyance and boezem storage. These relationships contradict a generic all-water interpretation of exact zero in the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset.

Programme and design documents establish mechanisms and planning, not current defence, pump, sluice, receiving-level, groundwater, sewer, backup-power, storage, damage or T+72 state. No standard redistribution licence or machine update cadence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — KNMI FDSN induced-earthquake origins and Groningen ground-motion semantics
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI rolling 365-day FDSN catalogue retrieved 2 September 2026; catalogue automatically updates when events are published; CC BY 4.0 default RDSA licence
supports: The bounded deployment contains five reviewed induced/triggered origins in GM1952: Sappemeer M1.5795 on 26 July 2026, Harkstede M0.9093, Overschild M0.4734 and two Woudbloem events on 16 December 2025 at M0.4778 and M1.9899. Event parameters may be revised and are neither forecasts nor a ground-motion/damage surface.

KNMI explains that Groningen ShakeMaps for induced events above magnitude 2.0 combine measured station acceleration and a Ground Motion Prediction Equation; peak acceleration also depends on local soil. A source origin alone cannot justify one deterministic municipal g-value or building/service damage curve.

A controlled canonical earthquake replay with epicentre [6.801, 53.176] at the reviewed Sappemeer source produces 0.160723 g, 23,869 affected resident-equivalents at T+6, yet its containing CBS neighbourhood Sappemeer-Noord ranks fiftieth of 91 behind a cross-hazard seed order.

The source covers 365 days and a national bounding box and is CC BY 4.0. No catalogue point means no origin in that time/space query, never zero induced seismic hazard; an origin is static/timestamped observation evidence, not scenario likelihood or future occurrence.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Adopted risk/effects profile, 2025–2028 crisis plan, local ramp-plan facilities and 72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Beleidsplan Crisisbeheersing 2024–2028 adopted 12 July 2024; Regionaal Crisisplan 2025–2028 adopted 4 April 2025; current public pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted regional profile covers sea/regional flooding, drought/heat, nature fire, extreme weather, earthquakes, transport and chemical accidents, large fires, energy, drinking-water, ICT/telecom and cyber disruption. It expressly says real impact depends strongly on the selected scenario and local conditions and avoids false quantitative probability ranking.

The authority's current facility page identifies Avebe and Plixxent at Foxhol and J. Wildeman Storage & Logistics at Hoogezand among facilities with ramp-response plans, updated every eighteen months. A named regulated site is not evidence of a release, inventory, plume, occupancy, plan activation or resource availability.

The regional 72-hour preparedness campaign warns of prolonged electricity, drinking-water or internet loss and recommends household water, food, light, batteries and special supplies. Advice is neither measured household preparedness nor municipal stock/shelter capacity.

VRG earthquake guidance notes that Groningen earthquakes continue after Groningen-field extraction stopped in April 2024 and gives protective actions for injury, gas, water and electrical damage. Guidance/plan publication is governance evidence, not action completion or service restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / Provincie Groningen / RIVM / Ommelander Ziekenhuis
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road, rail, transit and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; RIVM questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph has eleven cross-boundary links: A7 toward Groningen and Oldambt; N33 toward Eemsdelta and Veendam; N386 and N962 toward Tynaarlo; N987 toward Eemsdelta; N865, N860 toward Groningen; and N385/N963 toward Veendam. Consecutive same-corridor sections are series, not additive emergency capacity.

ProRail places Hoogezand-Sappemeer, Martenshoek, Kropswolde and Zuidbroek stations inside GM1952 and the GTFS snapshot contains 173 stop areas. Static geometry and best-effort schedules do not establish train/bus operation, crossing/bridge passability, rolling stock, passenger counts, accessibility, capacity or restoration.

RIVM assigns no acute-care department inside GM1952. Nearest straight-line reference-point locations are Ommelander Ziekenhuis Scheemda 10.656 km, UMCG 15.541 km and Martini 16.576 km, all reported 24/7 with acute obstetrics. Straight-line distance and annual registered roles are not ambulance time, route availability, live occupancy, acceptance, staffing, generator endurance or T+72 capacity.

The Province documents the A7/N33 corridor through Hoogezand and Zuidbroek and has shown that severe winter conditions can close N33 and suspend bridge/sluice operation on regional waterways. Historic disruption establishes a mechanism, not a current closure or future state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RWS Waterinfo / KNMI
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, grid planning, communications, education and bounded observation context
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 438 GM1952 points: 54 surface-water pumps, 19 sewer pumps, six sluices, two wastewater-treatment points and 357 weirs. Capacity is present for 32 pumps and 17 sewer pumps, absent for all sluices, treatment points and weirs; units/connectivity, settings, current operation, reserve and backup remain unavailable.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Enexis service area KWD Kropswolde and reports 123.5 MW existing withdrawal/injection plus planning demand, queues and five projects from 2030. One at-least-quarterly/monthly planning sample, with exact dataset licence unidentified, is not municipality coverage, live load, outage, switching, reserve or topology.

RDI returns 161 antenna installations: 57 mobile, 49 fixed-link, nine broadcast and 46 amateur; DUO returns 42 education-location records. Register presence does not establish coverage/backhaul/power, shelter designation, occupants, accessibility, supplies or live operation. RDI's reuse licence/cadence is unstated; DUO is daily CC Attribution, version unspecified.

No RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI weather-station observation, NDW situation or RIVM acute-care point is assigned inside GM1952 in the bounded snapshots. Nearest Slochtersluis observation was stale and publisher-flagged possibly faulty; Delfzijl forecasts and Eelde weather are external point context. No match remains NoData, never normal water/weather, open routes or available care.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — 't Roegwold nature exposure and event-valid wildfire/readiness context
evidenceSources.edition: Current public pages inspected 3 September 2026; Groningen nature-fire phase messages dated April–June 2026; no blanket reuse licence identified
supports: Staatsbosbeheer places the approximately 1,700-hectare 't Roegwold in Midden-Groningen between Kolham and Appingedam, comprising Westerpolder, Ae's Woudbloem, Dannemeer, Tetjehorn and Haansvaart with reed marsh, peat lakes, woods and grassland open year-round on paths.

VRG moved Groningen to nature-fire phase 2 after prolonged drought on 25 June 2026 and explains that fire may spread quickly and unpredictably; this is time-bounded regional readiness context, not a September incident or a local ignition/perimeter.

Brandweer Groningen's July 2025 access/firewater policy says nature-area incidents require accessible routes suitable for fire vehicles and situation-specific measures. Policy does not establish present access, water, crew arrival, suppression progress or containment.

A focused canonical wildfire source at the Slochteren Natuurgebied centre produces direct fire 0.395497, smoke 0.417856 and 7,660 affected resident-equivalents at T+24, yet the source neighbourhood ranks fifteenth behind the same shared order used by storm, pluvial, heat, winter, cyber and coastal cases.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, geography and resident totals reconcile.

findings.action: Retain the authoritative code/name/boundary and source values, the 17-person reconciliation difference, field-level null semantics, editions and licences. Do not rewrite rounded source observations.

findings.summary: The flood presets select neither Midden-Groningen's Duurswold pathway nor an authority-reviewed sea/canal/boezem case.

River is exactly zero at all checkpoints although official evidence documents polders 2–3 m below NAP, raised Slochterdiep/Afwateringskanaal/Schildmeer boezem, pumps and discharge toward Farmsum.

Relabel exact river zero as only no Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct forcing; keep Duurswold, Eemskanaal, Winschoterdiep, canal-dike, polder, seepage, pluvial and drainage states Unknown until modelled.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected Hunze en Aa's/RWS/WMCN/LIWO event supplies boundary water level/datum, defence or canal-dike state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM1952.

The exact Rhine/Meuse/IJssel zero says nothing about Duurswold, Slochterdiep, Afwateringskanaal, Schildmeer, Eemskanaal, Winschoterdiep, polder, regional-defence, seepage, sewer, groundwater or pluvial pathways.

The 438 HWH points are a partial contributor aggregation and lack complete catchment connectivity, flow direction, unit-compatible capacity, settings, receiving levels, current state, backup and restoration.

KNMI event origins are timestamped source observations, not ground-motion, felt-intensity, damage, probability or forecast surfaces; no reviewed event-specific ShakeMap/GMPE, soil/site, building/asset fragility or inspection state is selected.

No public source establishes a current 't Roegwold ignition/perimeter, fuel moisture, local wind/plume, visitor presence, route/firewater, crews or suppression state. Regional phase messages are time-bounded readiness context.

Named ramp-plan facilities do not publish incident inventories, plume, occupancy, alarm, protection, dependency or response-resource state suitable for direct simulation; sensitive facts must not be reconstructed.

Eleven road-border links use nominal scenario units and omit current bridge/crossing, four-station rail, transit, rural last-mile, ambulance, mutual-aid and destination state; same-corridor series sections are not additive.

No RIVM acute department lies inside GM1952. Straight-line proximity to Scheemda/Groningen does not establish ambulance travel, passable route, acceptance/diversion, staffing, beds, power/oxygen, generator fuel or T+72 throughput.

One NBNL Enexis planning sample, a recent successful Meeden reroute and 161 RDI sites do not establish municipal/national electricity or telecom topology, coverage, live load, outage, backhaul, backup, reserve or restoration.
CBS residents exclude workers, pupils, patients, visitors, responders and displaced people; no privacy-safe event-time presence, care-demand or assistance-needs layer is integrated.

No in-boundary Waterinfo, KNMI weather, NDW or acute-care point match is a bounded coverage result. External/stale/faulty points and missing records remain NoData, never normal conditions, open access or safety.

Exact hazard, affected-population, eight-service, recovery and person-hour results remain synthetic exercise outputs, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments until critical/high findings are corrected and reviewed by local authorities.

This audit covers the first 72 hours only; structural strengthening, flood recovery, repairs, displacement, environmental/industrial effects and psychosocial consequences can last substantially longer.
